Redefine_Guidelines: Product requirements must be clearly defined, customer-facing, and focus on visible touchpoints or insight-driven needs.
Requirements must be measurable and specify clear metrics; avoid vague statements such as 'Equal or better than Predecessor'.
Do not include best practices or general process documentation as requirements.
Channel requests for feature, experience, and warranty improvements to the appropriate function owners (Marketing, GxD, TME) for holistic assessment.

In_Scope_Product_Specific: Performance/Feature requirements specific to the product.
Quality Improvement & Serviceability that is unique to the product.
Documentation and Process directly related to the product.
Test Setup / Fixture needs unique to the product.
Design For Manufacturing (DFM) that is product-specific.
Cost Reduction initiatives directly impacting the product.
Out_of_Scope_Common_Across_All_Products: Safety & Regulatory compliance (applies to all products).
Environment & Sustainability compliance (applies to all products).
Hardware Reliability that is not product-specific.

Threshold_Target_Guidelines.Guideline: Requirement threshold/target must be specific, measurable, and avoid referencing 'Equal or better than Predecessor'.
Threshold_Target_Guidelines.Rationale: Vague statements like 'equal or better than predecessor' are difficult to measure and do not define clear expectations. Requirements should be stated from the customer perspective with actionable and measurable targets.

Example_Case_1_Tire_Mark.Challenge: Difficult to write technical specs for subjective issues (e.g., pick tire mark on photo media).
Example_Case_1_Tire_Mark.Proposal: State what the customer expects instead of vague reference.
Example_Case_1_Tire_Mark.Threshold: Minor tire mark acceptable (metric to be defined with program).
